articles.title: Donald Trump arremete contra LeBron James: "Le falta el respeto a nuestro país"
articles.standfirst: El presidente de Estados Unidos critica a la leyenda de la NBA por su actitud durante la ceremonia del himno previa al Knicks-Sixers
articles.summary: El presidente de Estados Unidos critica a la leyenda de la NBA por su actitud durante la ceremonia del himno previa al Knicks-Sixers
articles.body: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, cargó este jueves nuevamente contra la leyenda de la NBA Lebron James, al que criticó por no guardar una actitud solemne cuando sonó el himno nacional antes del partido que su equipo jugó en Nueva York el pasado martes. "¡Mientras suena nuestro himno nacional, LeBron James le falta al respeto a nuestro país! Dije desde el principio que no vale nada; es una vergüenza total!", escribió Trump en un mensaje en redes sociales que acompañó de un vídeo en el que se ve durante el himno a James ensayando, sin balón, el tiro, así como su swing de golf. "¡LeBron James debería pedir disculpas a todos esos grandes guerreros y héroes estadounidenses que murieron por la bandera de Estados Unidos y por todo lo que nuestro país representa!", añade el mensaje del presidente estadounidense. Trump ha cargado en numerosas ocasiones contra el baloncestista de los Sixers de Filadelfia, que también ha criticado con dureza al magnate inmobiliario. En septiembre de 2017, durante el primer mandato de Trump, James descalificó al magnate neoyorquino después que éste retirara su invitación para que los Golden State Warriors visitaran la Casa Blanca a raíz de que Stephen Curry -un conocido crítico del republicano- se opusiera a asistir. El exjugador de los Cavaliers, Heat y Lakers, que ha apoyado públicamente a todos los candidatos que han competido con Trump en unas presidenciales, escribió entonces en redes sociales "¡Ir a la Casa Blanca era un gran honor hasta que usted apareció!" El presidente estadounidense ha acusado a su vez a James de ser poco inteligente o incluso racista y ha aprovechado para decir que considera mejor jugador a Michael Jordan. En el primer partido de la que es su vigésimo cuarta temporada, James, de 41 años, logró el martes 14 puntos y nueve rebotes en la victoria de su equipo ante los Knicks, vigentes campeones de la NBA, en el Madison Square Garden.

articles.title: Karl-Anthony Towns Says He Must Do 'Better Job' of Avoiding Foul Trouble After Knicks' Loss to 76ers
articles.summary: New York Knicks star Karl-Anthony Towns knows he can't afford to be whistled as early as he was in Tuesday's season-opening loss to the Philadelphia 76ers once his team is back on the court.
articles.body:
New York Knicks star Karl-Anthony Towns knows he can't afford to be whistled as early as he was in Tuesday's season-opening loss to the Philadelphia 76ers once his team is back on the court.

Towns told reporters that "I have to do a better job to make sure I'm available for my team."

KAT logged the fewest minutes (24) of any Knicks starter, and that was due partially to the fact he picked up his second foul at the 8:46 mark of the first quarter. Coach Mike Brown immediately subbed him out for Andre Drummond.

Towns got his third foul with four minutes left in the first half, and that inevitably influenced how he played for the remainder of the contest.

The Sixers were in a similar position with big man Joel Embiid, who committed three fouls across a quick stretch in the second quarter.

Philly could at least make a tactical pivot by having LeBron James shift to the 5.

"I suggested that to the guys, the coaching staff, because I just felt like the way they were calling fouls, I just felt like — and I was just being honest — I wasn't going to be as aggressive as I should be on defense, having three fouls, wanting to stay on the floor," Embiid said, per ESPN's Dave McMenamin . "I just told them I thought we should do that."

That's not something New York can do as easily with starting power forward OG Anunoby. In addition, the Knicks don't have the same center depth they once did after Mitchell Robinson signed with the Boston Celtics.

Towns isn't what you'd consider a foul-prone player. He has averaged 3.4 per game across his career. Game 1 didn't present what should be a troublesome problem all year in that regard.

More than anything, KAT's foul trouble underscored what the reigning champions lost with Robinson's exit.

articles.title: Trump accuses LeBron James of 'disrespecting' US anthem
articles.summary: The basketball star recently appeared to be practising a golf swing and basketball shots while the national anthem was performed.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump has said basketball star LeBron James disrespected the US by not being still while the national anthem was sung.

James, who now plays for the Philadelphia 76ers, appeared to be practising a golf swing and basketball shots as the anthem was being performed ahead of the season-opening match against the New York Knicks on Wednesday.

"While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country!" Trump posted on social media. "LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag."

James has not responded to the president's latest comments but the pair have criticised each other in the past.

James can be seen in a video making the motion of a golf swing as a performer sings the Star-Spangled Banner at New York's Madison Square Garden.

His teammates, who are lined up next to him on the court, mostly remain standing with minimal movement.

"I said right from the beginning that he's no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE," Trump added, referring to James. "LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!"

The BBC has contacted James for a response through the 76ers and has also asked the team to comment.

The US anthem is played or performed at the start of most professional sports games. Players and spectators are expected to stand for it, if they can, and refrain from moving around. Some people sing along.

This tradition has become a political flash-point before. In 2016, former American football player Colin Kaepernick sat down and later knelt on one knee during the anthem as a demonstration against police brutality and racism in the US.

Trump criticised Kaepernick and later took credit when the athlete could not find a team to play for. Years later, he softened his stance saying Kaepernick should "get another shot" to play in the NFL.

The president has had a longstanding feud with James, who has publicly endorsed or campaigned for Trump's political opponents since the 2016 presidential election

In 2018, Trump suggested James was not intelligent after the athlete said he "would never sit across" from him.

That same year, James accused Trump of giving racists "an opportunity to be out and outspoken without fear".

He has also suggested that Trump's rhetoric led to a mob storming the US Capitol in 2021 to stop the certification of the result of the 2020 election, which former President Joe Biden won. James had endorsed Biden.

In July, when asked to choose between James and Michael Jordan as the all-time greatest basketball player in history, Trump said he preferred Jordan.

"I only like people that like me," Trump said.

James, 41, is the highest point scorer in the history of the National Basketball Association league with more than 40,000 points. He has had a long career and has won the NBA championship with every team he has played for.

In July,⁠ he signed a two-year contract with Philadelphia which is widely expected to be his last as a professional player.

articles.title: Carmelo Anthony Says Wemby Didn't Show 'Any Developed Skill Sets' in Spurs' NBA Opener vs. Thunder
articles.summary: After Victor Wembanyama recorded arguably the worst offensive game of his NBA career in the San Antonio Spurs' season-opening loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder, a Basketball Hall of Famer is asking what he worked on in the offseason.
articles.body:
After Victor Wembanyama recorded arguably the worst offensive game of his NBA career in the San Antonio Spurs' season-opening loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder, a Basketball Hall of Famer is asking what he worked on in the offseason.

On the latest episode of his 7PM in Brooklyn podcast (starts at 38:59 mark), Anthony pointed out he didn't see "any developed skill sets" from Wembanyama after watching him shoot 1-of-13 from the field against the Thunder:

"What have you worked on skill set-wise?… Again, this his first game, but in that first game, I didn't see any developed skill sets. I saw what he was trying to do. He was trying to get to the elbow, trying to get to the mid-post face-ups. I see that, but the skill set, I'm waiting to see that. That's what my eye going to be on this year for Wemby."

In the aftermath of the Spurs' loss in the NBA Finals to the New York Knicks, The Athletic's Jared Weiss wrote about Wembanyama's offseason and aspects of his game he worked on.

One of them included a highlight from the Spurs showing Wembanyama doing the "Dirk Fade," a reference to the one-legged jumper made famous by Dallas Mavericks legend Dirk Nowitzki.

"It's an important step in one of his main offseason training priorities: developing a more robust post game," Weiss wrote, adding Wembanyama also worked with Hakeem Olajuwon for the second straight summer.

When you make only one of 13 shots, it's going to be eye-opening. But perhaps the most jarring part of that stat line is that Wembanyama was 1-of-6 in the paint.

With the Spurs trying out a new three-guard lineup featuring Dylan Harper, De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle that will take time to gel, Wembanyama was supposed to be the stabilizing force for the offense.

Instead, Wembanyama looked like part of the problem for the Spurs on that end of the floor. It's only one game against arguably the best defensive team in the NBA, so the panic meter shouldn't be high right now.

However, since Wembanyama has made it no secret he wants to be viewed as the face of the NBA and a global superstar, there's going to be more scrutiny on you for games like this against the team viewed as your biggest rival.

As long as Wembanyama uses that game as a learning experience and corrects what wasn't working, this will be a blip on the radar. If his shot still doesn't fall on Friday when the Spurs host the Houston Rockets, the questions about his offensive versatility will only get louder.

articles.title: Carmelo Anthony Says 'It's Very Clear' 76ers are Tyrese Maxey's Team After Win vs. Knicks
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers have no shortage of star power this season, but it is clear who the leader is going to be on the offensive side.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers have no shortage of star power this season, but it is clear who the leader is going to be on the offensive side.

At least in the eyes of Hall of Famer Carmelo Anthony.

"It's very clear whose team it is," Anthony said of Tyrese Maxey on the latest episode of 7PM in Brooklyn (26:50 mark). "It's Maxey's team. This team is going to go where Maxey takes us."

Maxey is an offensive star, but it is still a head-turning statement considering one of the best players of all-time in LeBron James joined the roster this offseason. What's more, Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown are on the team, but Anthony highlighted how it can all work.

"For Bron to give Maxey those keys and take a step back, but don't even take a step back, he takes a step to the side … now he gets a chance to just be creative," Anthony said. " … That's when it gets scary."

He also said "the East is in trouble" if it all clicks together early in the season without much time needed for adjustments.

And that seemed to be the case in Tuesday's opener when the 76ers defeated the reigning-champion New York Knicks 106-100 with Maxey taking over for stretches as a scorer on his way to a game-high 28 points, five assists, four rebounds, three steals and three blocks.

Brown (19 points), James (14) and Embiid (13) also finished in double figures in a balanced scoring display that was surely troubling to the rest of the East.

After all, if the 76ers have already figured out a scoring balance in the first game of the season against the reigning champions, it only figures to get better as the season progresses and they all get more experience playing alongside each other.

That is especially true if Maxey continues to assert himself as the go-to option.

articles.title: Trump blasts 76ers' star LeBron James as 'disgrace' for not standing still during national anthem
articles.summary: PHILADELPHIA (AP) — President Donald Trump on Thursday accused LeBron James of disrespecting the United States after the NBA star appeared to continue his wa...
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA (AP) — President Donald Trump on Thursday accused LeBron James of disrespecting the United States after the NBA star appeared to continue his warmups while the national anthem was performed before Philadelphia's season opener on Tuesday.

"I said right from the beginning that he's no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE," Trump said of James in a social media post sharing the video. "LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!"

James appeared to practice a golf swing and jump shot as The Star-Spangled Banner was performed at Tuesday's game in New York. James, starting his first season with Philadelphia, was lined up alongside teammates who mostly stood still during the anthem.

Trump and James have been critical of each another for years, occasionally trading public swipes.

James had not made a public comment or a social media post as of Thursday afternoon about Trump's gripe.

The 41-year-old James, in his record 24th NBA season, was set to make his home debut for the Sixers Thursday night against Cleveland.

Among some of the more notable times James became entangled with the president or politics:

James was with Cleveland in 2017 when he made a statement during an NBA game with his shoes — one black, one white , with the word "equality" in capital gold letters on the back of each.

Then, after the game, James made a statement about Trump, saying: "This is a beautiful country and we're never going to let one person dictate how beautiful and how powerful we are."

James had called Trump " a bum " on Twitter and also said earlier that season of the president: "He doesn't understand how many kids, no matter the race, look up to the president of the United State for guidance, for leadership, for words of encouragement. He doesn't understand that, and that's what makes me more sick than anything."

James showed determination to speak out on social issues and the nation's political climate after Fox News host Laura Ingraham criticized the four-time NBA champion for his 2018 comments about social issues.

"We will definitely not shut up and dribble ," James said. "I will definitely not do that. I mean too much to society. I mean too much to the youth. I mean too much to so many kids that feel like they don't have a way out and they need someone to help lead them out of the situation they're in."

James referenced Muhammad Ali, Jim Brown, Bill Russell and Jackie Robinson as athletes who previously spoke up for equality and change with no concerns about the consequences or any rewards.

"We know it's bigger than us," James said.

James was named The Associated Press' Male Athlete of the Year in 2020 in large part for leading the Los Angeles Lakers to a championship and helped convince many — at the peak of Black Lives Matter — who had never voted to finally head to the polls.

"I still know what I do on the floor and obviously, I give everything to the game," James said. "But I can make a greater impact off the floor right now, more than I can on the floor. And I want to continue to inspire people with the way I play the game of basketball. But there's so many more things that I can do off the floor to help cultivate people, inspire people, bring people together, empower them."

James rejects Zlatan's criticism of activist athletes

AC Milan striker and former LA Galaxy star Zlatan Ibrahimovic blasted socially conscious athletes in a 2021 interview. Ibrahimovic called it "a mistake" for James and other athletes to get involved in political causes, saying they should "just do what you do best, because it doesn't look good."

James, naturally, rejected the criticism.

"I would never shut up about things that are wrong," James said.

AP White House reporter Collin Binkley in Washington contributed to this story.

articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news, and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Over the hump and safely into another big week(end) of football. And baseball! Sure, Rays-Brewers ain't exactly Mets-Yankees from 2000, but the Fall Classic is still the Fall Classic. Lord knows it's better than the whatever it is they're doing in the WNBA at the moment. Thank goodness that season is just about over. Goodness, it'll be nice when the curtains close on that league here in a few days. It'll be smooth sailing after that! Just football, baseball, hockey and the NBA ... if you so choose. Beautiful time of year. Let's roll. Welcome to a Thursday Nightcaps — the one where LPGA star Charley Hull throws her bikini in the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit ring for the first time. LPGA STAR CHARLEY HULL HAS FRIEND TO THANK FOR NOT GETTING DRUNKEN FOREHEAD TATTOO AFTER NIGHT OUT AT THE CLUB That's right. I've got Pat McAfee's first ESPN alt-cast of a Monday night game going terribly, the big-wigs over at NASCAR HQ experiencing a similar situation, and we've got more national anthem drama ... somehow. The president has even weighed in this time! I'll be honest with you, I have national anthem drama fatigue. I'm just over it. I don't care anymore. Beyond the obvious disgust, do you guys care anymore? I'm curious. OK, grab you your favorite horror movie in anticipation of tomorrow's National Horror Movie Day, and settle in for a Thursday 'Cap! THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! There's nothing scary about Charley Hull! Those of you who have been in this class since the beginning (nearly five years now!) know that I'm a horror movie buff. I love that stuff. I grew up watching scary movies with my mom. In fact, she accidentally took me to a screening of Rob Zombie's Halloween II as a teenager, and the whole movie basically just turned out to be a bunch of sex scenes. We didn't talk for two days. Anyway, I maintain that Halloween is the greatest horror movie of all time. It's certainly the best slasher movie out there. The theme song. The suspense. The ridiculous sequels and spin-offs. It's just perfect. The entire franchise is great, except the most recent movie, which was trash. Mount Rushmore of Halloween movies? Sure, why not?! Honorable mentions: Halloween 6 (Paul Rudd's debut!) and the first Halloween of the most recent reboot trilogy. The other two STUNK. LPGA STAR CHARLEY HULL DITCHES THE LINKS FOR A BIKINI GIRLS TRIP, DOLPHINS-BENGALS FAN FIGHT & 'BAMA NO-CALL! And that concludes the cinema portion of today's class. You're welcome! OK, let's get this thing started with someone who is the opposite of scary: LPGA star, Charley Hull! Turns out, our girl is dipping her toe into the SI Swimsuit waters: McAfee's alt-broadcast was a dud From Sports Illustrated: Professional golfer Charley Hull will make her SI Swimsuit debut in the 2027 issue. After turning pro in 2013, Hull quickly became the youngest player to ever represent Europe in the Solheim Cup at the age of 17. Now 30, the English golfer is a three-time LPGA Tour winner who reached her career high of No. 3 in the Rolex Women’s World Golf Rankings in February 2026. Welcome to the show, Charley Hull! OutKick has been following Hull since the beginning, so it's good to see her getting the credit she deserves. She may be European, but make no mistake about it ... she's a patriot. Check out what she said to Joe Kinsey last month about Sydney Sweeney's gambling ad that sent the left into a death spiral: "The amount of backlash that (it) is getting, I just don't understand the way people's brains work. They're making a big deal out of nothing. It's an actress slash model modeling for an advert. And I think she owns the company as well." Yep. I think she'll do just fine in her new endeavor. Worse comes to worst, she'll certainly do better than Pat McAfee's alt-broadcast of Monday Night Football earlier this week: TV problems, anthem fatigue & NASCAR's red flag So, here's the thing ... A lot of folks say those embarrassing ratings are a sign that fans have "Pat McAfee fatigue." I disagree. I think we have "alt-broadcast fatigue." WHY do we need multiple broadcasts of a game? I don't get it. You go to watch a college football game on ESPN nowadays, and you accidentally end up watching the "Skycast" view, which is just an announcer-less view of the game from a camera above the action. That's it. WHY do we need that?! Why do we need an "alt-cast"? Just give us the stupid game on the stupid channel and leave us alone. We don't need to hear what another group of analysts thinks of the game. We don't need to watch the game from their sideline perspective. We don't need a "Next-Gen" broadcast of all the stats nobody cares about. Just let us watch the game! It ain't McAfee fatigue. It's streaming fatigue. That's it. Don't believe me? Ask NASCAR! Look at that number! Do you understand how bad that is? Sunday's NASCAR playoff race at Phoenix drew just 1.2 million viewers. That's unfathomably bad. I wrote about it this morning and really got into the weeds. I won't do that here because we all have better things to do, but feel free to dive in. Bottom line? NASCAR's top series has been on network TV all of seven times this year. Seven. That means the other 26 races have been on either cable, or streaming. That ain't gonna work. Again, folks are tired of the extra nonsense. We've gone too far with streaming and alt-broadcasts. Simpler is better. NASCAR is now learning that the hard way. Finally, on the way out, let's check in on the latest national anthem scandal on the hardwood: I'd like to leave the class with a question today ... Are y'all over the anthem stuff? I don't mean that in a bad way. I'm not saying it's not ridiculous behavior, because it is. But do we really care how LeBron James acts before games? Is it really worth getting upset over LEBRON JAMES in 2026? Or at the insufferable WNBA girls? We know who they are. We know what they believe, and how they act. articles.title: Paul George draws NBA season's first fine for flopping after league reviews Celtics-Pistons game
articles.summary: During the offseason, the NBA said it would emphasize 'secondary, theatrical and exaggerated movement' with flopping fines for the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
Paul George had a historic debut with the Boston Celtics on Tuesday that later earned another notable footnote.

George, 36, tallied 38 points in Boston's 121-113 loss to the Detroit Pistons, setting a franchise record for most points scored in a Celtics debut. Additionally, he shot 7-of-12 on 3-pointers, passing Kyle Korver for eighth on the NBA's all-time 3-point shots made list.

Following the game, George drew the season's first fine for flopping on a fourth-quarter collision at midcourt with Detroit's Duncan Robinson. No call was made during the game, but the league issued a $2,000 fine after reviewing the play.

The postgame penalty was part of the NBA's emphasis this season to crack down on "STEM" violations — or Secondary, Theatrical, Exaggerated Movements attempting to draw foul calls.

"It's just something that we've seen that doesn't present well in-game, live or on TV, and it's not the fabric of NBA competition," NBA executive vice president and head of basketball operations James Jones said in a statement issued by the league . "We're going to take a really hard stance on flopping. It's something that we'll look at more so than anything."

NBA senior vice president and head of referee development and training Monty McCutchen clarified that the exaggerated effort to get a call is what will earn fines from the league, not necessarily the attempt to draw a whistle.

"A flop is not merely trying to entice a call. It has to be secondary, theatrical and exaggerated movement," he said. "A lot of these embellishments won't have that STEM — secondary, theatrical, exaggerated movement — and thus would be legal." "Creating a perception of something that you know not to be true, that is separate and needs to be penalized," he added.

"A flop is not merely trying to entice a call. It has to be secondary, theatrical and exaggerated movement," he said. "A lot of these embellishments won't have that STEM — secondary, theatrical, exaggerated movement — and thus would be legal."

"Creating a perception of something that you know not to be true, that is separate and needs to be penalized," he added.

Under the new initiative, if a player is called for flopping in a game, he will receive a non-unsportsmanlike technical foul and the opposing team gets a free throw. But if the flop is not called during the game, as in George's case, the league can issue a decision after reviewing the play.

Players who continue to get punished for flopping will draw an increased amount for a fine and could be issued a one-game suspension after six or more flopping penalties.

George was last fined for flopping during the 2023-24 season while with the Los Angeles Clippers, according to Spotrac . During his previous 16 NBA seasons, he's been fined a total of $300,000. That does not include $11.7 million he was docked for being suspended for 25 games without pay last season for violating the league's anti-drug program.

articles.body: El Real Madrid firmó su séptimo triunfo seguido entre Liga y Euroliga con una convincente victoria en el exilio del Maccabi en Belgrado (93-113) en la que tuvo que ofrecer lo mejor de su repertorio para remontar 15 puntos de desventaja (44-29, min 15). En cuanto apretó en defensa jugó más liberado en ataque y su exhibición triplista acabó sepultando a los israelíes. Pedro Martínez no se cansa de pedir a sus chicos que tiren más triples, y esta vez le hicieron caso batiendo el récord del Madrid en la Euroliga con 21/39 (su anterior plusmarca era de 19), anotando y lanzando más incluso que tiros de dos puntos (12/29). Fue un festival ofensivo comandado por un formidable Campazzo (21+3+5 con 5/7 triples), que dirigió la orquesta blanca como en sus mejores tiempos, secundado por la garra de un Feliz que no se cansa de morder (18+2+4 con 4/8 triples), el poderío interior de Tavares (11+7+2 tapones) y un Luwawu-Cabarrot que volvió a parecerse a él mismo (15+3+2 y 3/7 t3). Entre todos hicieron estériles los esfuerzos de Clark (20+4+3), Colson (19) y Madar (14+3+5). El arranque de los blancos, con Jantunen hiperactivo y Tavares dominando bajo tableros, fue prometedor (5-7), pero fue sentarse el gigante caboverdiano y desmelenarse los israelíes, que encontraron una barra libre bajo el aro madridista que exprimieron Brisset, Howard y Sorkin (19-12, min 7). Luego Dibartolomeu, Sorkin y Clark capitalizaron la segunda oleada para disparar al Maccabi (26-17), acertadísimo en sus tiros (10/12 t2 y 3/6 t3) ante la lamentable anuencia defensiva del Madrid, que favoreció el acierto rival (30-23, min 10). Los triples de Smith y Jantunen parecieron espolear a los blancos, pero fue un espejismo. Theis sacó de sus casillas a Tavares anotando siete puntos por rapidez y lejanía, y Colson y Madar se subieron a su carro para poner la máxima para los locales (44-29, min 15). Entraron en escena entonces Feliz y Luwawu-Cabarrot para encender la mecha de la remontada con sus triples. El francés, tras varios partidos desaparecido, recuperó su mejor versión para comandar un parcial de 7/22 con dos triples y siete puntos suyos, tres de Feliz y uno de Campazzo (52-51, min 20). Vendaval ofensivo sustentado en una notable mejoría defensiva. En la reanudación Tavares y Luwawu-Cabarrot llevaron la voz cantante para poner a su equipo por delante (56-58), pero el Maccabi se aferró al partido con un triple de Brissett y seis puntos de Madar (63-62, min 25). Campazzo agitó otra vez su varita y con ocho puntos y dos triples lideró el arreón definitivo con un parcial de 5-19 culminado con cinco puntos de Abalde (68-81, min 29). El Maccabi renació con dos tiros libres de Clark y un triplazo sobre la bocina de Colson, que acercó aún más a los suyos al inicio del último acto (75-81, min 31). El Madrid volvió a la carga con una canasta y un 3+1 de Feliz, pero el Maccabi reaccionó a los mordiscos del Tigre de Guachupita con cinco puntos de Clark y un triple de Colson (85-91). El Madrid siguió exprimiendo su idilio con el triple y con uno de Okeke y dos de Abalde quebró definitivamente la resistencia israelí y acabó arrasando (93-113). 99 – Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv (30+22+21+26): Wallace (3), Madar (14), Hoard (10), Brissett (10), Theis (9) -cinco inicial-; Clark III (20), Sorkin (5), Dibartolomeo (5), Leaf (2), Colson (19), Bacot (2), Rayman (-). 113 – Real Madrid (23+28+30+32): Maledon (11), Feliz (18), Jantunen (6), Okeke (6), Tavares (11) -cinco inicial-, Smith Jr. (5), Campazzo (21), Pradilla (2), Luwawu-Cabarrot (15), Abalde (15) y Jones (3). articles.title: El Barça se arma de paciencia para llevarse la victoria de Milán
articles.standfirst: El conjunto azulgrana dominó de inicio a fin el partido ante Armani pero tuvo que sudar hasta el final para llevarse un triunfo trabajado en un gran partido coral
articles.summary: El conjunto azulgrana dominó de inicio a fin el partido ante Armani pero tuvo que sudar hasta el final para llevarse un triunfo trabajado en un gran partido coral
articles.body: El Barcelona consiguió llevarse la victoria de Milán en un gran partido coral de todo el equipo que tuvo que sufrir hasta el final. La aportación ofensiva por tramos de distintos jugadores como Parra, Martin o Punter y el desempeño en ambos lados de la cancha de otros como Gibson o Nebo fue determinante para apuntarse la cuarta victoria de la temporada en esta Euroliga. Los de Aleksander Sekulic arrancaron con un ritmo alto de juego que les hizo ponerse con un 7-14 de salida, liderados por un Joel Parra que anotó sus dos primeros triples. La rotación rompió el orden y el Barcelona frenó su anotación, que sólo anotó cuatro puntos en los siguientes cinco minutos. Fue el propio Parra el que cortó la sequía con una bandeja y anotó un palmeo sobre la bocina del primer cuarto para marcharse en ventaja (21-23) y ponerse con 10 puntos. El segundo periodo no tuvo nada de acierto. El parcial era de 5-3 llegado prácticamente al ecuador, hasta que Tyrese Martin anotó cinco puntos consecutivos para lanzar ligeramente al equipo blaugrana de nuevo en el marcador (29-34), culminado con un gran alley-oop entre Justin Robinson y Olivier Nkamhoua. Fue entonces cuando se impuso un poco más la defensa culé y el rebote ofensivo a través de Josh Nebo, pero dos canastas de Bolmaro cerraron la brecha (40-44) al descanso. En la reanudación, el Barcelona amenazó con recuperar la máxima de ocho puntos (40-47) pero cinco tantos consecutivos de RJ Cole volvían a acercar a los italianos. El primer triple de Punter, que no tuvo su día desde el 6,75 (2/8) acompañó a los de Robinson, Gibson y Umude, y una buena secuencia posterior de Nebo bajo el aro puso la máxima (52-66) a falta de 2:48 para el final. Sin embargo, en un cuarto con alternativas para ambos, Darius Thompson volvía a colocar a cuatro puntos a los suyos (64-68) antes de que Umoja Gibson metiera un triplazo sobre la bocina para calmar los nervios. En los últimos diez minutos se mantuvieron las distancias, con un tres más uno de Punter incluido para sofocar el momento de inspiración de Burnell (15 puntos y 4/5 en triples) que amenazaba con acercar a Olimpia Milan. Tras cinco minutos de tira y afloja, llegó el momento de Umoja Gibson para reventar el partido. Cuatro puntos seguidos y varias acciones defensivas positivas pusieron el 69-83 a 4:08 que provocó el desfile del pabellón de la afición local. Finalmente el Barcelona consiguió conservar la ventaja y cerrar su cuarta victoria en esta Euroliga con un partido trabajado. 81 - Armani Milan (21-19-24-17): Cole (9), Hall (5), Mathews (3), Peters (13), Wright (6) -cinco inicial-, Burnell (15), Diop (-), Bolmaro (12), Thompson (12), Ricci (-), Guduric (2) y Booker (4). 89 - Barcelona (23-21-27-18): Robinson (10), Punter (17), Martin (14), Parra (12), Balcerowski (0) -cinco inicial-, Gibson (13), Umude (7), Nkamhoua (4), Núñez (-), Evbuomwan (0), Minaya (1) y Nebo (11). articles.standfirst: Los griegos reaccionaron a tiempo para seguir siendo líderes de la Euroliga
articles.summary: Los griegos reaccionaron a tiempo para seguir siendo líderes de la Euroliga
articles.body: El Panathinaikos reaccionó a tiempo este jueves para superar a un serio Kosner Baskonia, que estuvo cerca de dar la sorpresa en Atenas, donde cayó con honores por 85-79, en el último minuto de la séptima jornada de la Euroliga. Los azulgranas miraron de tu a tu a uno de los grandes candidatos al título en un choque del que no se desconectaron en ningún momento y tiraron de los menos habituales para seguir el ritmo del interminable equipo de Zeljko Obradovic. Mathias Lessort hizo mucho daño en la pintura visitante y fue el mejor con 20 puntos y seis rebotes. Por el lado azulgrana, Tadas Sedekerskis fue el más regular con 10 puntos y cinco rebotes, hasta que se retiró con problemas físicos. Matteo Spagnolo apareció cuando más lo necesito el equipo y Stefan Joksimovic y Clement Frisch rozaron la heroica en el último cuarto. Los griegos anotaron con más comodidad en un partido que comenzó con igualdad, pero donde Nigel Hayes-Davis tiro del equipo local con nueve puntos consecutivos. Las pérdidas de balón hicieron mucho daño a los azulgranas, que controlaron el rebote y pudieron seguir el paso del Panathinaikos, que mantuvo el nivel físico con su larga rotación. El Baskonia logró ponerse por delante, 20-21, a pesar de que los helenos no fallaban sus tiros de dos, que llegaban desde el dos contra dos. El rebote ofensivo le dio más oportunidades al conjunto dirigido por Zeljko Obradovic, que colapsó la zona baskonista para volver a dominar. Las faltas rigurosas y las pérdidas de balón cayeron como una losa sobre la plantilla vitoriana, mientras los verdes despertaban poco a poco. Pero el Baskonia salió muy bien de la presión del Panathinaikos y apoyados en un gran Tadas Sedekerskis y la dirección de Damion Baugh continuó al acecho al descanso, 43-40, a pesar de las 12 pérdidas de balón de la primera parte. La combinación entre Sylvain Francisco y Mathiass Lessort castigó al conjunto vasco en el inicio de la segunda mitad, pero Matteo Spagnolo con siete puntos consecutivos sostuvo a los baskonistas. El italiano, que aprovechó la ausencia de Kobi Simmons, no tuvo más apoyo anotador y la distancia creció hasta los diez puntos. Los azulgranas sufrieron en su zona y no pudieron igualar el físico de un Panathinaikos que entró en el último asalto con un 63-54 a favor. Los problemas físicos de Tadas Sedekerskis complicaron aún más la rotación de los vitorianos, que se agarraron de nuevo al partido con Clement Frisch y Stefan Joksimovic. Un 2-13 para los de Velimir Perasovic voltearon el marcador y dejó al Baskonia por delante con seis minutos por delante, pero la calidad individual de los verdes y el rebote ofensivo recuperó sensaciones para los locales. Francisco volvió a encontrar a Lessort, se volvió a estirar la ventaja, pero el Baskonia no se arrugó, volvió a empatar a 79, con 1:26 para el final, pero dos triples de Panathinaikos cerraron el partido, 85-79. 85 - Panathinaikos (20+23+20+22): Francisco (10), Badio (3), Hayes-Davis (18), Hernangómez (-) y Mitoglu (8) -cinco inicial-, Yabusele (9), Nunn (11), Fall (1), Lessort (20), Grant (5) y Bonga (-). 79 - Kosner Baskonia (21+19+14+15): Baugh (8), Spagnolo (16), Stewarrt (-), Kurucs (-) y Faried (6) -cinco inicial-, Lawson (8), Sedekerskis (10), Joksimovic (13), Frisch (11) y Santos (7). Árbitros: Robert Lottermoser (Alemania), Marcin Kowalski (Polonia) y Saso Petek (Eslovenia). Sin eliminados. Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la séptima jornada de la Euroliga, disputado en el pabellón Telekom Center (Oaka) de Atenas.

articles.title: Trump slams NBA's LeBron James for national anthem actions
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump lashed out at NBA superstar LeBron James on Thursday for what he called disrespectful behavior during the playing of the national a...
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump lashed out at NBA superstar LeBron James on Thursday for what he called disrespectful behavior during the playing of the national anthem.

Trump posted a video of the basketball legend doing apparent warm-up movements while lined-up with his Philadelphia 76ers teammates.

"While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he's no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE," Trump wrote on his Truth Social network.

"LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!" he wrote.

The video used by Trump had an internal caption that read: "LeBron working on his golf swing pregame." It showed him doing lateral swing motions and basketball shooting movements.

It was not immediately clear when the video was filmed.

There was no immediate reaction from James, 41, who is entering a record-extending 24th NBA season with his fourth team, or the 76ers.

Trump has been critical of athletes before -- particularly Black athletes -- for their behavior during the playing of the US national anthem before games.

During his first term, Trump singled out NFL star Colin Kaepernick for his decision to kneel during the "Star-Spangled Banner" to protest at racial injustice and police brutality.

articles.title: Basketball, BBQ and Georgia coach Ayla Guzzardo's Louisiana upbringing
articles.summary: Hi-Ho Barbecue has been a staple in Georgia women's basketball coach Ayla Guzzardo's family for 70 years. Here's how it came to be.
articles.body:
Check out our Georgia football vs Auburn photo gallery: Best images

If you're ever in Hammond, La., and desperate for a pulled pork sandwich made with love, head over to Hi-Ho #1 Barbecue , owned (partially and silently, she emphasized) by none other than Georgia women's basketball head coach Ayla Guzzardo.

Hi-Ho Barbecue has been a staple in the Guzzardo family for 70 years.

Growing up, they used to cook the meat in their backyard. They also make their own sauce, though Guzzardo wouldn't share the secret recipe with us. Just know it's so good that Georgia athletic director Josh Brooks, also from Hammond, has been bugging her to bring some back for him next time she visits home.

"If you know anyone from the area, they love it," Guzzardo said.

Today, while she and her little sister jointly received her dad's portion of ownership when he passed away, it's mostly run by manager Zach Russell — who's also been a staple in the family forever.

"He is phenomenal," Guzzardo said of Russell. "My grandpa actually chose him to be the first person to offer to buy it. He keeps the Guzzardo legacy in. He's never changed anything."

Russell was unavailable for comment at the time this article was published.

Guzzardo said she'd always wanted to own a restaurant, that was her end goal, not coaching, but growing up, girls weren't allowed to work at Hi-Ho Barbecue — "pawpaw's rules," she said. She'd go to work with them as a kid, maybe get the chance to clean trays and wipe tables, but that was the extent.

"Girls didn't need to be in front of the counter," she recalled. "We protect our women. Women stay at home and they cook in the South. It just is what it is. Men go to work. We protect our women. They stay at home. That has always kind of been his mindset. When my dad started owning it, it trickled in a little bit, but my little sister got to work there. I've always just been busy with basketball and everything else."

Her first "real" job was as a graduate assistant with Akron women's basketball. Now, she's in her fourth head coaching gig.

articles.title: Steve Kerr Reacts to Yaxel Lendeborg's Luka Doncic Trash Talk After Warriors' Loss to Lakers
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg and Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Dončić had quite the back-and-forth during Wednesday night's season-opener for both teams, with Lendeborg ultimately getting hit with a technical foul.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg and Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Dončić had quite the back-and-forth during Wednesday night's season-opener for both teams, with Lendeborg ultimately getting hit with a technical foul.

Golden State head coach Steve Kerr appreciated Lendeborg not backing down, with one small caveat:

Dončić ultimately had the last laugh, as the Lakers won 127-105 behind his 28 points, eight rebounds and seven assists. But Lendeborg—who held Dončić to 1-of-6 shooting from the field when he was the primary defender on him—had plenty to say about the Lakers' star after the contest.

"I had a lot of respect for him [because] I didn't really watch the NBA much," he told reporters. "I just watched highlights and seen him kill people. But being in it firsthand and seeing all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect. ... I guess this is what the NBA is like, man. A lot of flopping, a lot of foul baiting, a lot of praying to the refs, man. Interesting first game for me."
